items.title: ‘This is a life commitment’: Mississauga shelter drops pet adoption fees to just $25
items.summary: ​ Until Aug. 22, adopting a pet from Mississauga Animal Services is going down from $280 to $25. Manager of Animal Care and Wellbeing Greg Madeley told Now Toronto that the shelter has launched this promo due to a lack of space for strays, aiming to avoid overcrowding. He says he has been saddened by the number of pets living in the same kennels for years and hopes this initiative will finally allow them to find a forever home. “We don’t have the space to perform our job, which is to take in strays, because there’s no room for them,” he said. ” “We will absorb [the financial loss] so these animals can live in a proper home instead of a kennel,” Madeley shared. All pets have been neutered/spayed, microchipped, and vaccinated. Since the promotion started on Aug. 8, five of the 22 available dogs have been adopted over the weekend, and many cats have been adopted into loving homes. At the time of publication, one kitten remains up for adoption, and Madeley shared that more cats will be in the shelter before the promotion expires. Mississauga Animal Services is also offering pet lovers the opportunity to foster-to-adopt, where they can help an unwell animal get healthy; the shelter will cover the cost, and they can later adopt the animal if they fall in love with it.

items.title: Brampton suspect arrested in Mississauga stabbing
items.summary: Police have charged a Brampton man with aggravated assault after a victim was stabbed in Mississauga. The incident happened on Aug. 1 at a commercial unit in the area of Dixie Road and Aimco Boulevard in Mississauga, Peel Regional Police say. One adult male was stabbed and rushed to a local trauma centre in serious but stable condition and is expected to recover, police say. Investigators identified the suspect as Gregory Darling, 32, of Brampton and urged him to turn himself in. Police now say Darling was arrested on Aug. 2 and has been charged with one count of aggravated assault. Peel police say the accused was held for a bail hearing and attended the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton. Anyone with information about this incident can contact Peel Regional Police by calling 905-453-3311. ca. When you contact Crime Stoppers you stay anonymous, never have to testify, and could receive a $2,000 reward.

items.title: Man, 32, charged in Mississauga nightclub stabbing
items.summary: A man has been arrested in connection with a stabbing that took place outside a Mississauga nightclub during the August long weekend. On Monday, Peel Regional Police provided an update on the case and announced the arrest of 32-year-old Gregory Darling of Brampton. m. on August 1. When they arrived at the scene, police found a man suffering from multiple stab wounds. He was transported to a trauma centre for treatment. Footage from the scene shows what appears to be splatters of blood near the front entrance of Sugar Daddy’s Nite Club. Darling was subsequently arrested the next day and charged with a single count of aggravated assault. He was held for a bail hearing and attended the Ontario Court of Justice in Brampton.

items.title: Police officer cleared after man tasered at motel in Mississauga
items.summary: A Peel police officer was cleared of criminal charges connected to a man’s serious injuries after he was tasered in Mississauga. The province’s police watchdog, the Special Investigations Unit, investigated the incident and concluded there were no grounds for criminal charges. m. on April 25 this year, the SIU said. A Peel Regional Police officer encountered a suspected impaired driver in the parking lot of the motel, the SIU said in its report released today. The man was lying in the driver’s seat of a Jeep, which was parked with its lights on. The officer approached, knocked on the window and the man was initially unresponsive and then delayed acknowledging the officer when he appeared to wake and sat up in his chair, the report stated. The man asked the officer what he wanted and the officer said that he wanted to ensure the man was okay. The man said he was fine and walked away from the officer towards the front doors of the motel, ignoring the officer’s requests that he stop, the report stated. The SIU said the man became combative and punched the officer in the head before fleeing into the Hotel 6 lobby. The man was attempting to enter his room when the officer tasered him. Several other officers arrived to assist and the man was handcuffed.

items.title: Warning issued about Eventbrite listings falsely using City of Mississauga’s name
items.summary: The City of Mississauga is warning residents after two Eventbrite listings were found with false claims. The city became aware of the two Eventbrite listings for the International Conference on Leadership, Innovation, Global Investment, & Professional Development (ICLIGP), the city said in a press release. The listings falsely claim to be in partnership with the city and state that the event will take place at Malton Community Centre from Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 and Nov. 30, the city said. “The City is not affiliated with these events, and no booking exists for this at any City facility,” the city said. ” The city urged residents and businesses to verify event details before registering or purchasing tickets. One event was deleted from Eventbrite as of Monday. An event listed on Eventbrite claimed to be associated with the City of Mississauga.

items.title: This Mississauga mom had her skin cancer symptoms dismissed by dermatologists. A new clinic came to the rescue
items.summary: Liliya Leheta had a referral declined. A new program at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre diagnosed her within two weeks. Liliya Leheta at her Mississauga home. The mother of three and nail salon owner discovered a strange mole on her chest that continued to grow over time. But her symptoms were dismissed by dermatologists, and her referral to a specialist was declined. Liliya Leheta, a Mississauga-based mom of three, was out with her kids on a sunny day in March of 2023 when she realized she forgot to apply sunscreen. The next day, she noticed her skin peeling on her sternum, but thought little of it — until, less than a year later, she noticed a strange, red mole that suddenly appeared near the centre of her chest. A striking shift in demographics is worrying doctors who say it’s part of a wider trend showing steep increases of cancer in people under 50. A striking shift in demographics is worrying doctors who say it’s part of a wider trend showing steep increases of cancer in people under 50. Over the next two years, Leheta would watch in horror as the tiny red dot swelled, changed shape and bled. ” Then, in the fall of 2025, Leheta learned of a recently opened rapid assessment centre for skin cancer at Princess Margaret Cancer Centre. Within two weeks of her referral, she was seen and diagnosed with basal cell carcinoma — the most common form of skin cancer in Canada. Less than two months later, a surgeon successfully removed the cancerous tissue. Leheta remains cancer-free to this day.

items.title: Mississauga man dies after canoe capsizes in Ontario lake
items.summary: A man has died after a canoe capsized on a lake in the Muskoka area over the weekend. m. Saturday to reports of a capsized canoe on Stewart Lake in Georgian Bay Township. Investigators say two people were in the canoe when it overturned about 40 feet from shore. One occupant was rescued by a passing boater, while the other went underwater and did not resurface. Police say the missing paddler, a 31-year-old from Mississauga, was found dead on Sunday. The investigation is continuing with assistance from the Office of the Chief Coroner and the Ontario Forensic Pathology Service. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Bracebridge OPP at 1-888-310-1122. Anonymous tips can also be submitted to Crime Stoppers by calling 1-800-222-8477 (TIPS). The OPP is also reminding boaters and paddlers to wear a properly fitted lifejacket or personal flotation device, check weather conditions before heading onto the water and ensure all required safety equipment is onboard.
